results.name: QuartzLine: A working PDF viewer with a backdoor inside
results.description: QuartzLine, also tracked as CLOUDHAZE by Mandiant, is malicious software disguised as a functional Windows PDF viewer that conceals a backdoor enabling attackers to execute commands and deploy additional malware. The malware has appeared as paperline.exe and fielddesk.exe, signed with a legitimate but now-revoked EV code-signing certificate. Distribution occurs through malicious advertising, where users searching for unrelated content click ads and download the viewer from AWS S3 buckets. Once installed, QuartzLine establishes persistence through scheduled tasks and communicates with command-and-control infrastructure. Observed attack chains include Chrome data theft within one week of installation, followed by deployment of second-stage RATs like Caira and IronBark. The backdoor operates with user-level privileges and can execute arbitrary Windows commands.

results.name: ConnectWise (SkyKick) Vendor Credentials Abused in M365 Attacks
results.description: A Microsoft 365 API credential belonging to ConnectWise Cloud Backup (formerly SkyKick) was compromised and used to gain unauthorized access to customer M365 environments. The threat actor authenticated from IP address 144.172.64.128 on October 15, obtaining Microsoft Graph access tokens across hundreds of tenants. The attacker moved through tenants in sorted GUID order, suggesting automated targeting. In one instance, the ConnectWise Cloud Management MS Teams application elevated itself to Global Administrator and added credentials to other applications, including security tools. The activity began with password spraying against law firms on October 13-14, followed by role assignments in approximately 50 tenants, and culminated in widespread credential abuse. Nearly 1,000 Entra tenants showed sign-in activity from the malicious IP, with over 300 successful authentications. A second targeted wave focused on 16 tenants in policy, national security, trade, and critical mineral sectors.

results.name: CVE-2026-88771: Inside the Exploitation of a Critical NetScaler RCE Vulnerability
results.description: On September 27, 2026, Citrix disclosed CVE-2026-88771, a critical remote code execution vulnerability affecting NetScaler Application Delivery Controller and NetScaler Gateway with a CVSS score of 9.8. The vulnerability enables unauthenticated attackers to execute arbitrary commands without requiring optional features. CISA added it to the Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog following confirmed worldwide exploitation. Attackers employ a staged exploitation chain involving access-log poisoning, where malicious Base64-encoded payloads are staged in HTTP User-Agent headers, followed by authentication log poisoning using forged PPE failure messages containing shell commands. A vulnerable Perl diagnostic script then executes the poisoned commands with elevated privileges. Observed activities include web shell deployment, PHP enablement, and delivery of FreeBSD implants from infrastructure overlapping with CVE-2026-75650 exploitation targeting Adobe Commerce systems.

results.name: YuanKong RAT: the Android remote-control service that stamps its operators' names into every build
results.description: YuanKong is a multi-tenant Android remote access trojan whose dropper stores decryption keys in cleartext configuration files. The malware uses a two-key XOR scheme to unpack payloads signed with a shared certificate across all operator builds. Each build embeds operator account identifiers as hardcoded string constants, including account IDs, operator handles, and enrollment codes that are transmitted to command-and-control servers. Analysis of 110 dropper samples revealed 57 distinct payloads belonging to 42 different operator accounts. The RAT steals credentials through screen capture, accessibility service abuse, and overlay attacks while escalating privileges by self-pairing with the device's own ADB daemon to obtain shell access. It communicates via Socket.IO over WebSocket with a shared set of C2 domains.

results.name: An Analysis of Suo5-Based Tunneling and Pivoting Attack Techniques Through Case Studies
results.description: This analysis examines exploitation of Suo5, an HTTP/HTTPS-based tunneling tool, for pivoting attacks through compromised web servers to access internal networks. Suo5 relays TCP traffic and enables SOCKS5 proxy access to internal systems, supporting multiple transmission modes and environments including Java, PHP, IIS/.NET, and Nginx. Two deployment methods were observed: file upload exploitation on IIS servers through renamed ASPX files, and memory injection via Jenkins Script Console using Groovy scripts to register Suo5 as Servlet and Filter components. Key indicators include repeated POST requests in web logs, DLL files in Temporary ASP.NET Files directories, and PluginServletFilter chains in Java logs. Detection strategies recommend monitoring web request patterns, server-side behaviors, abnormal User-Agent headers, unauthorized URI access, and file modifications in web application paths, alongside restricting script execution capabilities and implementing network segmentation controls.

results.name: Inside Help TDS: Hotejka, Cloudflare Pages and Predictive Detection
results.description: Since April 2017, a Russian-language affiliate program called Hotejka, believed to be a rebrand of ROI777, has operated the Help Traffic Distribution System (TDS), delivering tech support scams to victims. The operation uses browser fingerprinting and geolocation to redirect users through compromised websites, malvertising, social media, and spam to fake Microsoft security alerts that lock browsers and display fraudulent phone numbers. When victims call, operators from call centers guide them to install remote desktop tools like UltraViewer, granting complete system access for ongoing exploitation. Since April 2026, Hotejka has created over 20,000 disposable domains on free Cloudflare Pages infrastructure, generating approximately 300 new domains daily. Affiliates including Balada Injector, Detour Dog, and DollyWay drive traffic to the TDS. Infoblox developed predictive detection algorithms that identify malicious domains approximately seven days before deployment, reducing customer exposure from 4% to 0.5...

results.name: BREAK THE SILENCE: Tracking Silent Lynx Through Exposed Infrastructure
results.description: Silent Lynx, a persistent cyber espionage threat actor, has conducted targeted intrusion campaigns against government ministries, diplomatic missions, and civil society organizations across Central Asia since 2024. The group focuses on high-value public sector organizations in Commonwealth of Independent States countries, leveraging spear-phishing campaigns through compromised government email accounts and malware staging via GitHub. Operations from late 2024 through 2026 reveal extensive infrastructure including exposed open directories, newly registered domains, and GitHub repositories. The actor employs lightweight reverse shells, PowerShell scripts, proprietary tools, and commodity utilities. Recent activity shows adoption of exploit-assisted delivery via CVE-2025-8088, expanding focus on Linux systems, and interest in FortiWeb vulnerability CVE-2025-25257. results.name: Don't Call Us, We'll Call Your APIs | TraderTraitor Backdoors Resurface on Victim With No Crypto Ties
results.description: In 2026, the DPRK-sponsored Lazarus subgroup TraderTraitor continued campaigns targeting cryptocurrency entities, including a high-profile attack on LayerZero resulting in $292 million theft from KelpDAO. Following this disclosure, an additional victim was identified: a smaller IT services provider in India with no cryptocurrency connections. The compromise involved a DevOps engineer targeted through fake job interview lures containing weaponized Terraform coding projects. Malicious GitHub repositories used typosquatted provider domains to deliver macOS backdoors FLATROOF and ROOFDECK when victims executed terraform init. The backdoors enabled reconnaissance, credential theft, and cloud environment escalation. One day after LayerZero's public disclosure, attackers deployed an updated stripped version of ROOFDECK and removed earlier implants. Activity continued until June 2026, suggesting the threat actor ultimately abandoned the intrusion after determining insufficient value from the smaller target.

results.name: ChainScript: Tracing a Node.js RAT Through the Blockchain
results.description: Blackpoint's Adversary Pursuit Group identified ChainScript, a previously unnamed Node.js remote access trojan discovered during ClickFix investigation. The malware disguises itself as legitimate software including Spotify, Zoom Workplace, and Microsoft Teams through malicious Windows Installer packages. ChainScript employs an EtherHiding-style C2 discovery technique utilizing a Polygon smart contract to dynamically locate active WebSocket infrastructure, enabling operators to rotate backend services without rebuilding agents. The RAT provides comprehensive remote access capabilities including interactive shell sessions, file operations, screenshots, payload deployment, cryptocurrency wallet discovery, remote JavaScript execution, self-update mechanisms, and cleanup functions. Multiple builds appeared under different names (ComponentTask33, UpdateDigital, HostShared, OrchidViolet66) while maintaining consistent core agent architecture. results.name: Lazarus luring employees with trojanized coding challenges: The case of a Spanish aerospace company
results.description: ESET researchers uncovered a Lazarus attack against a Spanish aerospace company where attackers masqueraded as Meta recruiters on LinkedIn, sending trojanized coding challenges to employees. The campaign deployed multiple tools including LightlessCan, a previously undocumented backdoor that mimics native Windows commands to evade detection. Initial access was achieved through spearphishing via LinkedIn Messaging, delivering malicious executables disguised as C++ programming tests. The attack chain involved DLL side-loading techniques delivering payloads including NickelLoader downloader, miniBlindingCan variant, and the sophisticated LightlessCan RAT supporting 68 commands. LightlessCan represents a significant advancement over its predecessor BlindingCan, implementing execution guardrails and enhanced stealth capabilities. The campaign targeted aerospace technology and know-how for cyberespionage purposes, consistent with North Korean strategic objectives in missile development.
